title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_0RD1LE_1RE1RF_1LC0RB_---1RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_0RD1LE_1RE1RF_1LC0RB_---1RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head shuttles out from the right end over the background word 1110111110, which it rewrites in a second phase and back (proved in Lean). It turns back at a defect or passes it depending on the defect's shape, and the excursions follow the ruler sequence of a binary counter whose bits are the defects. At the left end sits a unary counter (0111)^n: n grows by one at each of the rare events at that end (17 events between 3929 and 2.27·109 steps, n from 6 to 22). Between the ends, domains of another pattern grow at the right end and dissolve into gliders that travel left.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 64,251 cells have been visited and 50,921 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The sweeps over the background
claims.text: Right: B crosses (1110111110)^n in 22n steps, leaving (0111010111)^n; left: C crosses the same word, leaving (1101110101)^n; and the two rules that restore the word from the other phase (18n steps each).

claims.title: A unary counter at the left end
claims.text: Each time the left end grows (steps 3929, 5610, 11471, 15584, 50005, 101010, 405859, 851096, 2437041, 6477694, 16747343, 27831296, 79148713, 162337150, 471362435, 980924104, 2265696633) it grows by exactly one cell, and the tape there reads 0111 01 (0111)^n 0101… with n one more than at the previous event (n = 6 at 3929, 22 at 2265696633).

claims.title: Excursions follow a binary ruler sequence
claims.text: Between consecutive visits of the head to the right end in state B, near 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps, the head turns back after about 900, 15,600, 900, 22,900, 900, 15,600, 900, 28,500, … cells: the ruler sequence of a binary counter, each defect passing the head on every other visit.

claims.title: Domains and gliders
claims.text: In the defect picture, regions of a different pattern (black wedges) grow at the right end; when one stops growing, it is eaten from its left edge and sends gliders to the left; gliders slow down near the left end. The intervals between counter events grow irregularly (ratios 1.4 to 4).

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.049). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Next step: Identify the domain types at the right end and their erosion, the gliders they release, and how a glider increments the counter; then accelerate the run event by event.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps a unary counter at one end of its tape and a repeated 10-cell word everywhere else; patches of another pattern appear at the far end and dissolve into gliders, and every now and then the counter goes up by one.

facts.text: The head's sweeps over the two phases of the background, proved for every length.
The left-end counter at 2.3·10<sup>9</sup> steps, up by one per event.
No halt in the C simulator; 64,251 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A counter fed by gliders
html: Almost everywhere the tape repeats 0 1^3 0 1^5. At the right end, now and then, a patch of a different pattern starts growing with the tape (the black wedges). When a wedge stops growing it is eroded from its left side, and the erosion sends gliders to the left (the thin lines). At the left end the tape reads 0111 01 (0111)^n: a number n written in unary. It goes up by one at each event at that end:

A binary counter. The head does not cross the whole tape each time. Leaving the right end, around 2·108 steps, it turns back after about 900 cells on every other excursion, after about 15,600 on every fourth, 22,900 on every eighth, 26,600 to 29,500 on every sixteenth and beyond: the ruler sequence 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 4, … of a binary counter whose bits are the defects, each letting the head through on every other visit. The left end, and with it the unary counter, is reached only when every bit lets the head through: an overflow.

A halt needs F reading 0, which the background never offers. Whether some glider can bring the right pattern to the head is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.049). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).
After 109 steps the tape spans 64,251 cells (24 left of the start, 46,513 right), with a density of 1s of 0.793.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Glider collider with a unary counter (0111)^n at the slow end
summary: A bouncer over the period-10 background 0 1^3 0 1^5; the slow left end holds a unary counter (0111)^n that gains one copy at each rare event (n = 22 at 2.3*10^9 steps), fed by gliders and domains coming from the right end.
